key_insight: Thermal history, along with composition, controls hidden nanoscale octahedral-tilt domains in lead halide perovskites, which in turn alters their optoelectronic response.
engineering_relevance: Device performance and stability in perovskite solar cells may depend not only on chemistry but also on processing and temperature ramp rate during fabrication and operation.
method: Single-crystal X-ray and neutron diffuse scattering across Cs/MA/FA and Cl/Br/I compositions
Machine-learning-assisted molecular dynamics plus a phenomenological octahedral-tilt model
Hyperspectral photoluminescence to link local structure with optoelectronic response
evidence_signal: The abstract reports mapping of compositions through accessible phases and shows that heating rate alone changes photoluminescence quantum efficiency across the MAPbI3 phase transition.
watch_item: Thermal-history effects are likely processing-dependent, so results may not transfer directly between devices unless ramp rate and phase path are tightly controlled.
paper_title: Thermal history controls the optoelectronic response of lead halide perovskites through structure and dynamics
